d: Fatigue sets in and emotional cracks appear. Honest conversations about fear, frustration, and trust deepen their bond amid demanding survival tasks.
Limited resources force adaptation. Problem-solving, risk assessment, and mutual support become crucial as cooperation outweighs strength in the wild.
Nature tests their endurance and resilience. Harsh weather and terrain push limits, making survival a challenge of both body and mind.
Reflection marks the finale. The couple confronts how the wilderness reshaped them, revealing what truly matters when stripped of comfort and control.

Mario risks it all by rafting down the deadliest strip of water in Africa, the Zambezi River, towards lake Kariba, only to find himself in front of some of the biggest and baddest problematic man-eating crocodiles on the planet.
Mario was told by locals that deep in the Namibian desert there is an odd-looking creature that is great nutritional value that has been harvested by people for hundreds of years.
In the Kalahari Desert is an ancient tribe that has lived off the land since the beginning of man kind. These people are known as the Naru bushman.
Just off the coast of Africa is a strip of 115 islands called the Seychelles. Originally claimed by France in the 1700s most of the population speak French and the influence is felt in its cuisine.
When two oceans collide, there is mayhem on the horizon. On this episode Mario ventures off the coast of Cape Town where the Indian ocean meets the Atlantic.

Deep in the wilderness of Northern South Africa, poaching is rife, and the wilderness is as dangerous as it gets. Mario attempts to be the first person in the area to have ever harvested one of the most dangerous animals known to Africa.

The Axis deer populations in Hawaii have reached plague proportions and they are in-fact invasive to this beautifully pristine archipelago of the pacific. Luckily for Mario these deer also happen to boast the best tasting venison.
